findings.breaking_input: GET /v1/orders?receipt=... answers 200 with a non-JSON body (a proxy HTML page) or JSON with no `items` field. `rz` turns the parse failure into `body: null`, `list(undefined)` returns [], and `found` is empty.
findings.why: A check-then-create keyed on an unreadable answer reads as 'absent, create it'. Scaffold POSTs a second order even though launch's own order may already exist. The 'found before created' guarantee holds only when the list is well-formed.
findings.fix: Require `Array.isArray(body.items)` and `body.entity === 'collection'`. Otherwise throw an uncoded error before any POST.
findings.twin_of: A 404 from a token without access read as "absent, create it" -> every check-then-create keyed on a 404

findings.breaking_input: Two ventures with slugs sharing the first 29 characters (for example a 35-character slug and a 41-character slug with the same prefix). `receiptOf` cuts `arc-launch-<slug>` to 40 characters, so both get the same receipt.
findings.why: The receipt is cut but the slug regex still allows 41 characters. Venture B finds venture A's order, whose tag differs because the tag includes the slug. That reads as a foreign order and wedges venture B with FOREIGN_ORDER permanently. Distinct names are mapped onto one external name.
findings.fix: Cap the slug so `arc-launch-` plus the slug is at most 40 characters (slug at most 29), or refuse BAD_SLUG over the limit. Alternatively, put a short hash of the slug in the receipt.
findings.twin_of: Provider record names were guessed absolute-or-relative against the brand domain -> every name a provider returns: relative to WHAT?

findings.breaking_input: ctx.tag is undefined or an empty string, and the owner's order for launch's receipt has `notes: {}` or no `arc_launch_tag`. Then `o.notes.arc_launch_tag === ctx.tag` can be true.
findings.why: `ours()` compares against ctx.tag without asserting it is a non-empty string. With a missing tag, a foreign order is adopted as launch's, and verify passes on it. The ownership test also rests on a free-text notes field the owner can edit, with a guessable deterministic value.
findings.fix: Require `typeof ctx.tag === 'string' && ctx.tag.length > 0` inside `ours`. Refuse if the tag is unusable.
findings.twin_of: Ownership was a marker found anywhere in a user-editable description -> every ownership test on free text

findings.breaking_input: fetch aborted by the slot timeout throws a DOMException AbortError (name AbortError, numeric code 20). If ctx.fetch does not remap it to the string code ABORTED, `rz` rethrows it because `e.code` is truthy.
findings.why: `verify` rethrows only `e.code === 'ABORTED'`. A numeric-coded abort therefore becomes `{ok:false, reason:'20: ...'}`, so the slot timeout is swallowed as a verify failure. In scaffold it surfaces as a raw uncoded error. `if (e && e.code)` conflates coded refusals with any error carrying a code.
findings.fix: Test `e.name === 'AbortError' || e.code === 'ABORTED'` explicitly. Rethrow only string-coded launch refusals out of `rz`.
findings.twin_of: A sleep listened for "abort" on a signal that had already fired, so the slot timeout was swallowed for the whole poll

findings.breaking_input: State holds a razorpay-test-order resource whose id contains a newline or an ESC sequence (a hand-edited or corrupted state file). `teardown` prints `resource: r.id` verbatim.
findings.why: `probe` validates the id against the order_ regex and `say()`s adapter text, but teardown interpolates the state id raw. A terminal line can be forged.
findings.fix: Wrap `r.id` in `say()`, or filter to ids matching the order regex as `probe` does.
findings.twin_of: Adapter-supplied strings (resource ids, reasons, answerers) were printed raw, so a newline or escape could forge a line -> every terminal line that interpolates provider or adapter data

findings.breaking_input: Razorpay returns 400 for reasons other than a missing id (malformed request, or a transient BAD_REQUEST_ERROR). `verify` passes `allow:[400,404]` and treats any such status as 'razorpay has no order'.
findings.why: The reason text claims the order is absent, but a 400 does not prove that. Flipping a verified slot to not-ok with a wrong cause is the 'infer a cause from status' pattern.
findings.fix: Allow 404 only. For a 400, check that `error.description` names a missing id, or report 'razorpay refused the lookup (400)'.
findings.twin_of: Windows reports a SIGKILLed child as plain exit 1, so a reason built from the exit code named the wrong cause -> any code that infers a cause from `status` or `signal`
